duty: Subscribe to the EPR Programme including the Buy Back (Tenth Schedule)
duty_holder: importers, exporters, manufacturers, distributors, retailers, collectors, recyclers
evidence_quote: NESREA 'says it will begin enforcement of the Extended Producers Responsibility (EPR) guidelines and regulations' (D-G, 4 Aug 2026, Kano regulatory dialogue).
evidence_source: EnviroNews, 'NESREA to enforce EPR regulations against environmental pollution - D-G'
note: ARBR is registered as the battery-sector PRO (GIZ 2025 p.20; ThisDay 2026-04-24). No published count of subscribed producers was found. Leadership article 'only 128 firms comply' returned HTTP 403 and was not read.

duty: Contractors using batteries in public and private renewable energy projects comply with the EPR Programme
evidence_source: NESREA website, ARBR website, EPRON website, Federal Ministry of Environment, GIZ 2025, Nigerian press (searched 2026-11-05)
note: A pre-commencement record exists: REA adoption of EPR with a battery recycling fee per installed battery (Boell, 10 Dec 2021). No record after 21 March 2024 was found.

duty: Register with the Agency on the EPR Programme within one year of commencement (deadline 21 March 2025)
evidence_source: NESREA website, ARBR website, EPRON website, Federal Ministry of Environment, GIZ 2025, Nigerian press (searched 2026-11-05)
note: No public registration figures or register of battery producers were found. The Leadership compliance article (HTTP 403) could not be read.

duty: Put in place a collection system for used batteries; set up collection centres or take-back systems
evidence_quote: 'At the core of the programme is the deployment of specially designed collection receptacles across strategic locations in the Federal Capital Territory, including markets, schools, offices, and motor parks', implemented 'in partnership with the Alliance for Responsible Battery Recycling (ARBR)'.
evidence_source: ThisDay / Arise News, 'Nigeria launches nationwide drive to safely manage small battery waste'
note: The record covers small batteries in the Federal Capital Territory only; no nationwide record was found.

duty: Work with a Producer Responsibility Organisation for safe collection, treatment, transportation and disposal
evidence_quote: ARBR is 'the Producer Responsibility Organisation for Nigeria's battery sector' and partner in the FCT collection programme; NESREA's D-G gave a goodwill message.
evidence_source: ThisDay / Arise News, 'Nigeria launches nationwide drive to safely manage small battery waste'
note: The record shows the PRO operating a programme. The number of persons working with the PRO is not reported.

duty: Pay battery disposal and recycling fees to the PRO; PRO assesses and collects fees; PRO access to monies under guidelines
evidence_source: NESREA website, ARBR website, EPRON website, Federal Ministry of Environment, GIZ 2025, Nigerian press (searched 2026-11-05)
note: A pre-commencement ARBR page (Feb 2022) states that NESREA authorised fees, without amounts. No fee schedule, amounts or collection figures after 21 March 2024 were found. No fee amounts appear in S.I. No. 11 Reg. 11 or Schedules 10-16.

duty: Inform the Agency two weeks before selling used batteries
duty_holder: persons disposing of used batteries by sale
evidence_source: NESREA website, ARBR website, EPRON website, Federal Ministry of Environment, GIZ 2025, Nigerian press (searched 2026-11-05)

duty: Agency monitors and supervises the PRO
evidence_quote: Regulatory dialogue 'to clearly define the roles and responsibilities of stakeholders at the federal, state and local government levels in implementing the battery control regulations'.
evidence_source: EnviroNews, 'NESREA to enforce EPR regulations against environmental pollution - D-G'
note: No published report of PRO supervision was found.

duty: Submit an annual EPR report by 30 June (batteries sold, collected, processed or stored; processes; facility locations)
evidence_source: NESREA website, ARBR website, EPRON website, Federal Ministry of Environment, GIZ 2025, Nigerian press (searched 2026-11-05)
note: No published EPR annual reports or aggregate figures were found.

duty: At least one treatment facility in each of the six geo-political zones
duty_holder: producers placing batteries on the market
evidence_source: NESREA website, ARBR website, EPRON website, Federal Ministry of Environment, GIZ 2025, Nigerian press (searched 2026-11-05)
note: GIZ 2025 lists ten ULAB plants and maps those in Ogun State (Figure 2-3, p.12; Table 2-1, p.11) but does not give locations by zone (plants anonymised). No public record of facilities by zone was found.

duty: Carry out blood lead tests on facility workers at least twice every year
duty_holder: operators of used battery recycling plants
enforcement_source: NESREA press release 2025-11-28 (facilities sealed for failure to comply with S.I. No. 11)
evidence_quote: 'Currently, no such testing is conducted in Nigeria's ULAB recycling industry. In fact, most plants have never conducted any blood lead testing on workers or other stakeholders' (GIZ 2025 p.35). NESREA inspection (2025-11-28) found 'Absence of documented medical monitoring and regular blood-lead level testing for employees handling hazardous materials'.
evidence_source: GIZ 2025 ProBaMet Project Summary Report (S15), p.35
note: A7: recoded from 'public record of implementation found'; the sealing is recorded under enforcement_action. The basis is sector-wide: GIZ 2025 p.35 ('no such testing is conducted in Nigeria's ULAB recycling industry'). Ogun State announced free lead tests for residents and workers (allAfrica, 2025-12-01). Note: GIZ 2025 p.21 places blood-lead testing in Schedules 13-14; in the gazette it is in Reg. 48(1)(j), while Schedules 13 (B376) and 14 (B377) cover transport and recycling process controls.

duty: Environmentally sound transport (Sch. 13) and recycling, including battery breaking, acid and emission control (Sch. 14)
enforcement_source: NESREA press release 2025-11-28; Channels TV 2025-11-28 (seven facilities sealed)
evidence_quote: Violations include 'Improper battery breaking and acid management - Discharge of untreated lead-contaminated acid and effluents directly into the environment'.
evidence_source: NESREA press release, 'NESREA, Ogun State Govt. seal recycling facilities in Ogijo'
note: The record covers Ogijo facilities sealed on 2025-11-27/28. GIZ 2025 documents NESREA-led facility assessments (April and September 2024) and improvement plans (pp.14, 27). Scope (A7 follow-up): the evidence concerns the facilities sealed in Ogijo (NESREA, November 2025), not the sector as a whole.

duty: Slag and residues handled by the recycler with the PRO for environmentally sound disposal
evidence_quote: 'Under the protocol, the facilities committed to manage ULAB slag and base metal residue in a safe, environmentally sound and socially responsible manner'; inspections reported slag sold 'to residents and truck drivers for landfilling and construction'.
evidence_source: NESREA press release, 'NESREA, Ogun State Govt. seal recycling facilities in Ogijo'
note: Regulation number for the slag provision is inferred from its position before Reg. 8 (PDF p.7). Scope (A7 follow-up): the evidence concerns the facilities sealed in Ogijo (NESREA, November 2025), not the sector as a whole.

evidence_source: NESREA website, ARBR website, EPRON website, Federal Ministry of Environment, GIZ 2025, Nigerian press (searched 2026-11-05)
note: Cross-border inflows of used batteries are reported as illegal (Lead Battery Notes 2025; IDS 2016); this shows breaches, not a statement on implementation of the ban. No record of enforcement after 21 March 2024 was found.

instrument: S.I. No. 79 of 2022 (Electrical and Electronic Sector Regulations)
duty: PV panels within the scope of the e-waste regulations
evidence_quote: GEM 2024 p.64: in Nigeria 'the EPR system is private sector-led, operationalized by the E-waste Producer [Responsibility Organisation]'.
note: The record concerns the EPR system for EEE in general, not PV panels specifically.

instrument: S.I. No. 79 of 2022 (Electrical and Electronic Sector Regulations)
duty: Register with NESREA and the PRO (importers of new EEE, including PV panels)
evidence_source: NESREA website, ARBR website, EPRON website, Federal Ministry of Environment, GIZ 2025, Nigerian press (searched 2026-11-05)
note: EPRON's 'registered members' and producer-registration pages returned HTTP 403/500 on 2026-11-05. Search summaries describe solar companies among listed members, but this was not verified. No record specific to PV panel importers was read.

instrument: S.I. No. 79 of 2022 (Electrical and Electronic Sector Regulations)
duty: Subscribe to EPR and Buy Back (Eighth Schedule); take back end-of-life EEE and set up collection points; deliver to accredited recycler; importers pay for environmentally sound management
duty_holder: importers, manufacturers, distributors, retailers of EEE (including PV panels)
evidence_quote: UNIDO, EPRON and E-Terra 'have begun discussions on a possible collaboration' on 'the responsible management of solar panels, inverters, batteries and other renewable-energy equipment at end-of-life'.
evidence_source: The Tide, 'Stakeholders partner to tackle renewable energy e-waste'
note: No PV-specific take-back or collection record was found. An expert at a 2026-10-23 event said systems 'must be established to handle solar panels when they reach the end of their useful lives' (TheCable).
